1: # Worktree HUD Design
   2: 
   3: ## Product contract
   4: 
   5: `@scpz24/pi-worktree-hud` v0.1.0 is an independently installable Pi extension that keeps a non-capturing source-control HUD in the top-right of the live TUI viewport. It shows the current Git worktree, expands into a keyboard-driven file manager, supports file and repository-level stage/unstage operations, and opens a read-only file diff preview.
   6: 
   7: Supported baseline:
   8: 
   9: - Pi 0.84.1 or newer.
  10: - Node.js 22.19.0 or newer.
  11: - Git 2.23.0 or newer.
  12: - macOS and Linux.
  13: - TypeScript source distributed directly through `pi.extensions: ["./src/index.ts"]`.
  14: - No runtime dependencies beyond Node.js, Git, and Pi's public packages.
  15: 
  16: The implementation must not add commits, remotes, branch management, discard, checkout, reset, stash, hunk staging, file editing, watchers, private Pi APIs, ANSI cursor positioning, or a runtime dependency on `pi-breath`.
  17: 
  18: ## Architecture
  19: 
  20: ```mermaid
  21: flowchart LR
  22:     Events["Pi hooks / commands / shortcut"] --> Runtime["Session runtime"]
  23:     Keys["HUD keyboard"] --> Runtime
  24:     Runtime --> Refresh["Refresh controller"]
  25:     Runtime --> Queue["Index mutation queue"]
  26:     Runtime --> Overlay["Overlay controller"]
  27:     Refresh --> Git["Bounded Git runner"]
  28:     Queue --> Git
  29:     Git --> Core["Pure parsers and state reducers"]
  30:     Core --> Store["Bounded store"]
  31:     Store --> HUD["HUD component"]
  32:     Store --> Preview["On-demand diff preview"]
  33: ```
  34: 
  35: The code follows a functional-core, imperative-shell design:
  36: 
  37: - `git/` owns bounded child processes, repository probing, porcelain/numstat parsing, diffs, and exact mutation argv.
  38: - `state/` owns snapshots, row derivation, sorting, selection stability, list viewports, and footer precedence.
  39: - `runtime/` owns refresh generations, adaptive polling, the FIFO index queue, Agent mutation locks, and Overlay lifetime.
  40: - `tui/` owns compact/focused rendering, input mapping, width safety, and diff scrolling.
  41: - `index.ts` only registers Pi public events, the slash command, the global shortcut, and session-scoped runtime creation/cleanup.
  42: 
  43: Production code has no third-party runtime dependency. Every long-lived collection and output has an explicit upper bound.
  44: 
  45: ## Git and snapshot model
  46: 
  47: The extension checks `git --version`, discovers the root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, then runs all other commands from the canonical worktree root with `shell: false`.
  48: 
  49: Status is collected with:
  50: 
  51: ```text
  52: git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all
  53: ```
  54: 
  55: The NUL-streaming parser supports branch headers and record types `1`, `2`, `u`, and `?`, including arbitrary chunk boundaries and paths containing spaces, tabs, Unicode, or newlines. Branch headers determine normal, detached, and unborn display without additional per-refresh `symbolic-ref` processes. Unknown status letters are preserved. Unknown record types make the snapshot `partial`; parsed data remains visible but all index writes are locked.
  56: 
  57: Tracked statistics use NUL output:
  58: 
  59: ```text
  60: git --no-optional-locks diff --numstat -z --no-color --no-ext-diff
  61: git --no-optional-locks diff --cached --numstat -z --no-color --no-ext-diff
  62: ```
  63: 
  64: Binary entries increment `binaryFileCount` and do not contribute numeric additions/deletions. Untracked files never contribute to tracked statistics.
  65: 
  66: `WorktreeSnapshot` records generation, root, branch, HEAD existence, parsed files and HUD rows, counts, tracked statistics, completeness (`complete`, `truncated`, or `partial`), freshness (`current` or `stale`), capture time, and the last error.
  67: 
  68: Rows appear in the fixed order Conflicts, Staged, Changes, Untracked. Conflicts do not duplicate into ordinary sections. A partially staged path appears once in Staged and once in Changes because row IDs include section, current path, and original path. Section sorting uses a deterministic case-sensitive Unicode comparison.
  69: 
  70: ## Refresh and resource behavior
  71: 
  72: Compact, hidden, non-Git, and non-TUI states have no polling timer. Focused state has at most one adaptive timer:
  73: 
  74: - one-second status checks for the first ten seconds after activity;
  75: - three-second checks after ten quiet seconds;
  76: - five-second checks after thirty quiet seconds;
  77: - any input, Pi mutation hook, Git change, manual refresh, or completed index operation returns to one second.
  78: 
  79: Tracked dirty repositories refresh numstat at most every five seconds during polling. Explicit refresh triggers collect current statistics immediately.
  80: 
  81: Normal hook refreshes debounce for about 200 ms. Open, manual refresh, and mutation completion bypass the debounce. Only one read pipeline exists per runtime. A newer requested generation makes an older result ineligible to update the store. Refresh errors preserve the last snapshot as `stale`; browsing and preview remain available, while every index mutation remains locked until a complete refresh succeeds.
  82: 
  83: Status output is capped at 8 MiB and 5000 records. Diff output is capped at 2 MiB and 5000 lines. Preview data exists only while its modal exists. Shutdown prevents new work, clears timers, aborts child processes, permanently hides owned Overlays, disposes components exactly once, and releases cached data.
  84: 
  85: ## Index mutation semantics
  86: 
  87: All user index requests enter one FIFO queue, including repeated keys while an index operation is busy. Only one Git index command runs at a time. Each item performs a successful immediate refresh before the next item may execute.
  88: 
  89: File requests capture row identity, section/status, snapshot generation, and a lightweight precondition. Worktree/untracked/conflict requests capture an `lstat` signature; staged requests capture index status/OID information. A queued item is revalidated against the latest successful snapshot before execution. Changed or missing rows are skipped, and the footer reports the number of stale operations. All-operations are skipped if the snapshot generation changed after they were queued.
  90: 
  91: Exact commands:
  92: 
  93: - Stage file: `git add -- <path>`.
  94: - Stage all: `git add -A -- .`.
  95: - Unstage file with HEAD: `git restore --staged -- <path>`.
  96: - Unstage file on unborn branch: `git rm --cached -f -r --ignore-unmatch -- <path>`.
  97: - Unstage all with HEAD: `git restore --staged -- :/`.
  98: - Unstage all on unborn branch: `git rm --cached -f -r --ignore-unmatch -- .`.
  99: 
 100: Conflict rows may be staged after resolution. A conflict row cannot be individually unstaged, and any conflict in the snapshot disables Unstage All.
 101: 
 102: Agent `edit`, `write`, and `bash` executions are tracked by tool call ID. During this soft lock, new mutation requests are rejected and an existing queue pauses. The last mutating tool completion requests a refresh; staging unlocks only after that refresh succeeds. `agent_end` clears leaked tool IDs and refreshes. `agent_settled` is only a defensive cleanup path.
 103: 
 104: ## TUI and Overlay contract
 105: 
 106: The HUD Overlay uses `anchor: "top-right"`, width 52, `maxHeight: "60%"`, top/right margins of one, `nonCapturing: true`, and a visibility threshold of 72 columns by 12 rows. Row zero remains available to `pi-breath` without detection or imports.
 107: 
 108: Compact mode is at most four lines when dirty and three lines when clean. Widths at least 40 show the full layout; widths 28-39 drop statistics and secondary hints; narrower widths show only branch and a minimal change summary. Every rendered line is truncated by visible terminal width.
 109: 
 110: Both Compact and Focused modes draw a complete single-line frame inside the declared Overlay width. Compact frames use `borderMuted`; Focused frames use `borderAccent`. Non-zero additions use `toolDiffAdded`, non-zero deletions use `toolDiffRemoved`, and zero-valued directions are omitted. Staged, Changes, Conflicts, and Untracked headings and status codes use `success`, `warning`, `error`, and `accent` respectively, while paths remain normal text. Compact keeps branch and status but its only shortcut hint is `⌘R`.
 111: 
 112: Focused mode selects only file rows. Up/Down or j/k moves rows, Tab and Shift+Tab move between non-empty sections, Space stages or unstages the row, A/U enqueue all operations, Enter opens Preview, r refreshes, and Esc/q closes. The normal footer omits the refresh hint. Pi registers `Ctrl+R` and `Super+R` as open-only shortcuts: either mounts and focuses the HUD, and repeated use while Focused never closes it. All key matching uses Pi's public `matchesKey`/`Key` APIs.
 113: 
 114: Fullscreen transcript scrolling must leave the Overlay at the same screen-relative top-right coordinates. This is verified through public `TuiAltScreen` keyboard and mouse-wheel behavior. No ANSI positioning, private renderer access, input interception, or forced-render workaround is permitted for host-specific failures.
 115: 
 116: The long-lived `ctx.ui.custom()` call is fire-and-forget. The controller stores its own `OverlayHandle`, uses `focus`, `unfocus`, and permanent `hide`, never calls global `tui.hideOverlay`, and never uses `done` to close the HUD. Hiding destroys the component/handle; showing creates a new instance. Preview is a temporary topmost modal and may use `done`, then explicitly refocus the HUD.
 117: 
 118: ## Diff preview and path safety
 119: 
 120: Staged rows use cached diff; Changes and Conflicts use worktree diff. Diff lines do not wrap. Vertical, page, horizontal, and hunk navigation operate on bounded data, and each styled line closes its ANSI state.
 121: 
 122: Untracked files are inspected with `lstat`. Regular files are read up to 256 KiB and displayed as added lines up to 2000 lines. A NUL in the first 8 KiB marks binary content. Symlinks display only their link target and are never followed. Directories and other special files display a type summary. Absolute paths are resolved beneath the canonical root before any filesystem access.
 123: 
 124: ## Error and command behavior
 125: 
 126: Footer precedence is shutdown, Agent lock, stale/partial/Git error, current index operation and queue, refreshing, transient result, then normal key hints.
 127: 
 128: Git missing/old, non-Git, and non-TUI sessions do not mount or poll. Each startup error notifies at most once per session. Explicit show/refresh may re-probe. Repository disappearance clears state and removes the HUD.
 129: 
 130: `/worktree-hud status` reports repository, branch/HEAD, generation/capture/freshness/completeness, last error, active Agent mutations, current/queued index operations, poll interval, and Overlay state. Unknown subcommands show usage and never enter model context.
 131: 
 132: ## Packaging and validation
 133: 
 134: The HUD package uses Vitest 4.1.10, Biome 2.5.6, TypeScript 7.0.2, and fixed Pi 0.84.1 root development dependencies. Pi packages remain `"*"` peers. TypeScript checks produce no `dist`; the npm pack dry-run must contain only the manifest, source, README, and LICENSE.
 135: 
 136: CI runs the repository check on Node 22.19.0 on macOS and Linux. The initial functional package remains version 0.1.0 and creates no changeset or release.

1: # Worktree HUD Requirements-to-Tests Matrix
   2: 
   3: This matrix is the implementation acceptance contract for `@scpz24/pi-worktree-hud` v0.1.0. Automated tests use Vitest unless the row explicitly names the root Node scaffold contract or manual Pi acceptance.
   4: 
   5: | Requirement | Automated evidence | Manual evidence |
   6: | --- | --- | --- |
   7: | Pi 0.84.1 public API only | Typecheck against fixed 0.84.1; source scan rejects private fields/global Overlay hide | Load with `pi -e` |
   8: | Git 2.23+, canonical worktree root | Version/root integration tests including child cwd | Status command shows root |
   9: | Porcelain v2 NUL parsing | Fixtures for 1/2/u/?, multi-record, chunk splits, spaces, tabs, Unicode, newlines, unknown XY/type, truncation | Dirty repository layout |
  10: | Normal/detached/unborn branch | Real temporary repositories for all three branch states | HUD title inspection |
  11: | Section order and duplicate path rows | Row derivation tests for conflicts/staged/changes/untracked and staged+modified path | Partial-stage scenario |
  12: | Rename/current path semantics | Parser/row tests and real rename integration; mutation argv uses current path | Rename preview/stage |
  13: | Deterministic sorting and selection | Case/Unicode order, stable row ID, refresh preservation and fallback tests | Poll while navigating |
  14: | Bordered themed HUD | Responsive render tests cover complete frame, Compact/Focused border colors, diff colors, section/status colors, zero omission, plain paths, and visible widths | Inspect dark/light themes |
  15: | Compact HUD geometry | Responsive render tests; public TUI top-right/margin/row-one tests | regular/fullscreen visual check |
  16: | `pi-breath` coexistence | Memory terminal with dummy row-zero stripe | Run both extensions |
  17: | Focus and keyboard map | Component key tests and public Overlay focus tests; Ctrl+R/Super+R open only; Esc/q close; r refresh remains | Command+R, Ctrl+R, and slash fallback |
  18: | Fullscreen Overlay coordinates | Public `TuiAltScreen` plus memory Terminal verifies PageUp and mouse-wheel transcript scrolling preserve top-right screen coordinates | Scroll fullscreen transcript with mouse/trackpad |
  19: | File Stage/Stage All | Exact argv unit tests and real Git integration for add/modify/delete/untracked | Scenarios A/C |
  20: | File Unstage/Unstage All | HEAD/unborn integration; working-tree preservation | Scenario D |
  21: | Conflict safety | Conflict rows, file-unstage refusal, all-unstage refusal tests | Conflict repository |
  22: | FIFO index serialization | Fake runner proves max one mutation, busy requests queue in order | Rapid repeated keys |
  23: | Stale queued request safety | lstat/index precondition and all-generation skip tests | Modify queued path externally |
  24: | Agent soft lock | Parallel edit/write/bash IDs, reject/pause, successful-refresh unlock tests | Agent edit during Focused HUD |
  25: | Refresh generation and stale lock | Debounce, immediate, old result, error preservation, write-lock tests | Simulated Git error/recovery |
  26: | Adaptive polling/resource cleanup | Zero Compact timer, one Focused timer, 1/3/5 seconds, five-second numstat, shutdown zero tests | Observe no Compact Git polling |
  27: | Staged/unstaged diff | Real Git diff tests including delete, rename, binary, truncation | Scenario E |
  28: | Untracked preview safety | Text/binary/size/line/symlink/directory/path-containment tests | Open untracked text/binary |
  29: | Diff navigation | Vertical/page/horizontal/hunk/wide-line/ANSI tests | Keys in large diff |
  30: | Non-Git/non-TUI behavior | Fake context proves no Overlay/timer/status and once-only notification | Scenario G; text/rpc invocation |
  31: | Hide/show and TUI mode switch | Permanent instance hide, fresh show, disposal, no leaked timer/process tests | Scenario H |
  32: | Reload/session switching cleanup | Repeated shutdown/start fake Pi tests | `/reload`, `/new`, `/resume` |
  33: | Package independence | Root scaffold contract: peers `*`, no cross-dependency, independent manifest | `npm pack --dry-run` |
  34: | Publish contents and license | Pack JSON allowlist, no `dist`, MIT manifest/LICENSE tests | Inspect tarball listing |
  35: | macOS/Linux support | GitHub Actions matrix on Node 22.19 | Local macOS Pi acceptance |
  36: 
  37: ## Required parser fixtures
  38: 
  39: - Ordinary modified, added, deleted, type changed.
  40: - Rename and copy with original/current NUL paths.
  41: - Untracked, unmerged, and submodule status.
  42: - Staged plus unstaged status on the same path.
  43: - Spaces, tabs, Unicode, and newline-containing paths.
  44: - Unknown status letter, unknown record type, record-count/output truncation.
  45: - Branch headers for normal, detached, and initial repositories.
  46: 
  47: ## Required real-Git repositories
  48: 
  49: - Clean, unstaged, staged, staged-then-modified, untracked, deleted, renamed, conflicted.
  50: - Space and Unicode filenames; newline filename where the platform permits it.
  51: - Unborn branch and detached HEAD.
  52: - A cwd below the root.
  53: - Multiple linked worktrees proving operations remain in the selected worktree.
  54: 
  55: ## Manual Pi 0.84.1 acceptance
  56: 
  57: 1. Agent edit locks staging; tool completion refreshes; Stage moves a Changes row to Staged.
  58: 2. A staged file modified again appears in both Staged and Changes.
  59: 3. Stage All includes additions, modifications, deletions, and untracked paths.
  60: 4. Unborn Stage then Unstage preserves the file and returns it to Untracked.
  61: 5. Preview opens over the HUD, scrolls, closes with q, and restores HUD selection/focus.
  62: 6. A row-zero dummy `pi-breath` stripe remains intact while the HUD starts at row one.
  63: 7. A non-Git directory has no HUD or polling; explicit command gives one clear notification.
  64: 8. `/worktree-hud hide`, TUI renderer switch, and `/worktree-hud show` creates a fresh HUD without leaked Overlay/timer/process state.
  65: 9. Compact shows a complete muted border, branch/status, colored non-zero diff totals, and only the `⌘R` shortcut hint.
  66: 10. Focused uses an accent border and semantic section/status colors; `r` refresh works even though the normal footer omits it.
  67: 11. Fullscreen mouse/trackpad scrolling changes the transcript viewport while the HUD remains at the same top-right screen coordinates.

Implemented deferred refresh for hidden HUD state:

**mutations.ts changes:**
- Added `agentRefreshPending` getter for public access
- Added `refreshNow` parameter (default `true`) to `unlockAgent(id, refreshNow)` - when `false`, marks pending without starting refresh
